notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level), with no gate warning. Model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); no laser was attached and nothing here ran against hardware. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card reads this repository as a family-config SerialDriver over text commands (reason_code family:serial). The upstream builds every laser command from parts (cmd + '=' + str(value), vortran.py:189-192), so a serial command table cannot reproduce the wire lines the device receives (a table sends 'LE 1', the device receives 'LE=1'); the package is therefore a direct Driver over copylot.hardware.lasers.vortran.vortran:VortranLaser with a native.py factory, as the authoring guide prescribes for a command built from parts. NOT COVERED: the card's other four entry symbols and their devices are not served (ASIStage stage motion, FlirCamera camera images, BartelsUX7 pump, the optotune Board); in particular the camera image arrays (acquire_images, snap) are not carried by this package. NOT COVERED: of the laser wrapper itself the head identification (?LI), the current control (?LC), the pulse power (?PP), the external power control (?EPC) and the drive control mode (?C/?FC) are not exposed; the driver covers emission on/off, the power set point, the emission delay, the pulse mode and the fault status. The 5 second emission delay is exposed as a setting but not enforced by the driver (it is a device feature). UNITS: the clone names no unit for the laser power (the only nm/mW comments are in the garbled _identify_laser parsing, vortran.py:248-249), so the power fields are declared dimensionless (unit 1) and their descriptions say so. LIMITS: no text file of the clone states a power range and the maximum power is a property of the head (?MAXP), so the power set point is Limit.operator_required: hardware writes are refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until the site supplies site-limits.json (site-limits.example.json shows the overlay, which only narrows). RISK: the clone states no laser safety class, so the device risk is the card floor R1; a site whose head is above class 1 must raise the risk class in the registry before hardware use. The command syntax was not tried on a laser. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package; gate.digest is the digest the check printed.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-10-29; reviewed_by stays null): accepted after reviewer edits: risk raised from R1 to R2 (a laser above class 1; a class 3B or 4 head is R3, MHS/spec/04-safety.md), so the hardware backend waits for a human signature; native.py and facts.md now say so. The DEVIATION FROM THE CARD is accepted: a registry override now makes the card a direct driver. After the registry rebuild refreshed task.json, the reviewer re-ran the gate and wrote its digest above.
